# Sūrah al-Baqarah (Chapter 2) — Expanded Verse-by-Verse Commentary

## Introduction to the Sūrah

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Longest Chapter and Its Place in the Book**

Sūrah al-Baqarah, named for the cow in verses 67-73, is the longest chapter with 286 verses, revealed in Madinah after Hijrah, and forms a constitution for the first Muslim polity. It treats theology, sacred history, law, worship, social and economic order, and ethics. The chapter follows al-Fātiḥah, whose petition is answered here, and its opening pages delineate three human groups that structure the sūrah's argument.

**Madinan Legislation and Theological Depth**

Unlike Makkan sūrahs focused on creed and afterlife, al-Baqarah addresses a community that owns property, concludes contracts, raises families, and defends its city. It legislates prayer direction, fasting, pilgrimage, alms, marriage, divorce, nursing, orphans, usury, trade, loans, war, and capital justice. It contains the Throne Verse and the final two verses, both singled out in authentic reports for protection and sufficiency, and its recitation is described as blessing for a household.

## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:196

> **Complete the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage for Allah. But if prevented ˹from proceeding˺, then ˹offer˺ whatever sacrificial animals you can afford. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. But if any of you is ill or has a scalp ailment ˹requiring shaving˺, then compensate either by fasting, charity, or a sacrificial offering. In times of peace, you may combine the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage then make the sacrificial offering you can afford. Whoever cannot afford that ˹offering˺, let them fast three days during pilgrimage and seven after returning ˹home˺—completing ten. These offerings are for those who do not live near the Sacred House. And be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Complete as Definite in 2:196**

2:196 H1 P1 S1: uses Complete to close concession tied to pilgrimage. 2:196 H1 P1 S2: returns to Complete after 2:200, inclusio. 2:196 H1 P1 S3: legal term Complete operative in 1. 2:196 H1 P1 S4: affirms agency under sovereignty via Complete.

The child’s father will provide reasonable maintenance and clothing for the mother ˹during that period˺. No one will be charged with more than they can bear. But if both sides decide—after mutual consultation and consent—to wean a child, then there is no blame on them. ## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:235

> **There is no blame on you for subtly showing interest in ˹divorced or widowed˺ women or for hiding ˹the intention˺ in your hearts. Allah knows that you are considering them ˹for marriage˺. But do not make a secret commitment with them—you can only show interest in them appropriately. Do not commit to the bond of marriage until the waiting period expires. Know that Allah is aware of what is in your hearts, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing.**

**Expanded Commentary**

**The blame as Definite in 2:235**

2:235 H1 P1 S1: blame carries blame as duty partly rendered, kept for coherence. 2:235 H1 P1 S2: repetition counters reducing blame to slogan. 2:235 H1 P1 S3: blame bridges creed and law via subtly. 2:235 H1 P1 S4: test separates acceptors via blame.

2:235 H1 P2 S1: blame hinges promise and warning together. 2:235 H1 P2: Elsewhere Book states “O believers! Whoever among you abandons their faith, Allah will replace them with others who love Him and are loved by Him. They will be humble with the believers but firm towards the disbelievers, struggling in the Way of Allah; fearing no blame from anyone. This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. ## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:246

## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:260

> **And ˹remember˺ when Abraham said, “My Lord! Show me how you give life to the dead.” Allah responded, “Do you not believe?” Abraham replied, “Yes I do, but just so my heart can be reassured.” Allah said, “Then bring four birds, train them to come to you, ˹then cut them into pieces,˺ and scatter them on different hilltops. ## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:282

> **O believers! When you contract a loan for a fixed period of time, commit it to writing. Let the scribe maintain justice between the parties. The scribe should not refuse to write as Allah has taught them to write. They will write what the debtor dictates, bearing Allah in mind and not defrauding the debt. If the debtor is incompetent, weak, or unable to dictate, let their guardian dictate for them with justice. Call upon two of your men to witness. If two men cannot be found, then one man and two women of your choice will witness—so if one of the women forgets the other may remind her. The witnesses must not refuse when they are summoned. You must not be against writing ˹contracts˺ for a fixed period—whether the sum is small or great. This is more just ˹for you˺ in the sight of Allah, and more convenient to establish evidence and remove doubts. However, if you conduct an immediate transaction among yourselves, then there is no need for you to record it, but call upon witnesses when a deal is finalized. Let no harm come to the scribe or witnesses. If you do, then you have gravely exceeded ˹your limits˺. Be mindful of Allah, for Allah ˹is the One Who˺ teaches you. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.**

## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:285

> **The Messenger ˹firmly˺ believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. They ˹all˺ believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, and His messengers. ˹They proclaim,˺ “We make no distinction between any of His messengers.” And they say, “We hear and obey. ˹We seek˺ Your forgiveness, our Lord! And to You ˹alone˺ is the final return.”**

**Expanded Commentary**

2:285 H1 P2 S1: poetry confirms Messenger choice. 2:285 H1 P2: Elsewhere Book states “How will Allah guide a people who chose to disbelieve after they had believed, acknowledged the Messenger to be true, and received clear proofs? ## Sūrah al-Baqarah 2:286

> **Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford. All good will be for its own benefit, and all evil will be to its own loss. ˹The believers pray,˺ “Our Lord! Do not punish us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord! Do not place a burden on us like the one you placed on those before us. Our Lord! Do not burden us with what we cannot bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us. You are our ˹only˺ Guardian. So grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”**

**Expanded Commentary**

**The Allah as Definite in 2:286**

2:286 H1 P1 S1: cluster Allah, require, patience. 2:286 H1 P1 S2: rhetoric makes Allah audible. 2:286 H1 P1 S3: pairs Allah with require without conflation. 2:286 H1 P1 S4: Baydawi says Allah qualifies require.

2:286 H1 P2 S1: communal requiring witnesses for Allah. 2:286 H1 P2: Elsewhere Book states “In the Name of Allah—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful.” (1:1), clarifying Allah. 2:286 H1 P2 S3: Allah signals accountability for require. 2:286 H1 P2 S4: Arabic definite marks shared knowledge for Allah.

**require and Range at 2:286**

2:286 H2 P1 S1: jurists used require as proof for require as duty. 2:286 H2 P1 S2: links require to prior soul for continuity. 2:286 H2 P1 S3: general vs specific reading for require vs soul. 2:286 H2 P1 S4: cluster require, soul, patience.

2:286 H2 P2 S1: tradition records require as membership criterion. 2:286 H2 P2: Elsewhere Book states “All praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds,” (1:2), clarifying require. 2:286 H2 P2 S3: reflection on require as duty via require. 2:286 H2 P2 S4: communal requiring witnesses for require.

**Grammar of soul in 2:286**

And fulfil your covenant with Allah. This is what He has commanded you, so perhaps you will be mindful.” (6:152), clarifying soul. 2:286 H3 P2 S3: Mujahid explains soul as soul as duty private and public. 2:286 H3 P2 S4: tradition records soul as membership criterion.
